questions.title: Name an interface metaphor you used today.
questions.description: A word software borrowed from the physical world. One to three words. Add as many as you can think of.
questions.mergeHint: These tags name interface metaphors borrowed from the physical world. Merge two tags only when they name the SAME borrowed object or action ("trash" / "bin" / "recycle bin", "cart" / "shopping cart", "cut and paste" / "copy paste"). Never merge two different metaphors just because they come from the same place: "folder" and "file" stay separate, as do "desktop" and "window", "cloud" and "drive", "bookmark" and "tab".

questions.title: Where does that metaphor break down?
questions.description: Pick one metaphor and name the moment it stops matching the world it came from. One or two sentences.
questions.clusterHint: Cluster by the KIND of breakdown, not by which metaphor is mentioned. Useful kinds look like: the physical action is impossible (a file in two folders at once), the digital object does more than the physical one (emptying the trash is unrecoverable), two metaphors collide (dragging a disk to the trash to eject it), the source object is obsolete (the floppy-disk save icon), the metaphor hides a risk or a cost ("the cloud" is someone else's computer), the metaphor never covered the real task. Name each cluster with a short noun phrase naming the kind of breakdown, not a summary of the responses.

questions.title: The desktop metaphor: what is really going on?
questions.description: Pick the one closest to your view. We will disagree about this for ten minutes.
options: the computer pretends to be a desk
we reuse what we know about desks
neither a desk nor a file system
a 1980s leftover we are stuck with

questions.title: How do you make one thing on a screen stand out?
questions.description: Name a visual property you would change to pull the eye to it. One or two words.
questions.mergeHint: These tags name visual properties used to make an element stand out. Merge only spellings, plurals, and true synonyms of the same property ("colour" / "color", "white space" / "whitespace", "bigger" / "size", "bold" / "weight"). Never merge two distinct visual properties: "color" and "contrast" stay separate, as do "position" and "alignment", "size" and "shape", "motion" and "blinking".
